the chemical and spectroscopic properties, and thus the photometric properties of ellipticals formed by major disk-disk mergers, strongly depend on galactic masses.

more massive elliptical galaxies formed by more massive spirals tend to have larger metallicities, larger negative metallicity gradients, and larger radial Mg2 gradients, as well as larger M/LB ratios, redder central colors, and redder radial color gradients.
galaxy mergers can naturally reproduce the fundamental properties observed in ellipticals in a self-consistent manner if the progenitor-disk galaxies are sufficiently massive.
